description:
FILED s470br (Opus, 2026-09-05) while fixing #1115, which exposed it.
PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

`%p-std-slot` -- the ONE reading of "does this filehandle designator NAME a
standard handle" -- is blind to two spellings that DO name one:

  * a TYPEGLOB:      binmode *STDOUT, ':utf8';   open(*STDOUT, '>', $f);
  * a RAW name STRING (not boxed), which is what the TAP layer's
    `$builder->output` / `->failure_output` hand back.

`%p-install-fh` carries its OWN typeglob arm, so nothing crashes -- it keys the
stream under the glob's name in *p-filehandles* and NEVER dup2s onto the
descriptor.  So

    open(*STDOUT, '>', $file);   print "x\n";

re-points descriptor 1 in perl, while PCL installs a second stream under the
name and leaves descriptor 1 alone.  NOT probed against perl yet; do that
first.

WHY IT SURFACED: #1115 gave `binmode` a real implementation, and its
non-standard path DUPS THE DESCRIPTOR AND CLOSES THE ORIGINAL.  With the glob
spelling unrecognised, `binmode *STDOUT, ':utf8'` (t/uni/fold.t line 21) closed
descriptor 1 and the file lost all 928 of its rows to
`#<fd-stream for "descriptor 1"> is closed`.  s470br fixed THAT by deciding
from the DESCRIPTOR instead (`%p-std-descriptor`: a stream on fd 0/1/2 is a
standard handle whatever named it) -- deliberately NOT by widening
`%p-std-slot`, because that predicate is shared with `%p-install-fh` and
widening it changes what `open(*STDOUT,...)` does, which needs its own probe
and its own sweep.

WHAT TO DO: probe `open(*STDOUT,'>',$f)`, `open("STDOUT",'>',$f)` and a
raw-string designator vs perl 5.40.3, then widen `%p-std-slot` to every
spelling `%p-install-fh` has an arm for (the arms ARE the list) and let
`%p-rebind-std` do the dup2.  Bar: the gate plus the io/ companion leg,
because the change moves what a standard-handle reopen does.

=== DONE (s473f) ===
PROBED FIRST, as the task asked (5.40.3; the CHILD is the discriminator -- "it
went to the file" is true either way and only a dup2 makes `system("echo
child")` follow).  perl re-points the DESCRIPTOR for all of: *STDOUT, STDOUT,
\*STDOUT, a scalar holding "STDOUT", *STDERR, `binmode *STDOUT`, and
`open(*STDOUT,'>&',$log)`.

%p-std-slot answered only for a bareword SYMBOL and a box holding a name
STRING, so the four GLOB spellings registered a second stream under the name
and left descriptor 1 alone.  The reading of a designator now lives in
%p-std-name, covering every spelling %p-install-fh has an arm for.

THE NEGATIVE WAS A SILENT WRONG: the string arm stripped ANY package
qualifier, so `$n = "Foo::STDOUT"; open($n,'>',$f)` re-pointed descriptor 1
where perl opens THAT glob (probed).  A qualifier other than main:: now
disqualifies (%p-main-package-p).

s470br's %p-std-descriptor stays -- it answers a different question (a STREAM
on fd 0/1/2 is standard whatever named it), which a designator cannot.
Guard: 9 rows in Pl/t/handle-place-01.t, each run as a CHILD.  Commit f88ee7b0.
subject: %p-std-slot is blind to a TYPEGLOB and to a raw name string, so open(*STDOUT,..) installs a second stream instead of dup2ing descriptor 1 (found by #1115, worked around there by deciding from the descriptor)
